chapter: Own groups, bebop and Savoy sessions
title: The Cu-boppers octet and Latin percussion; reaction to bebop

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Why did you decide to add two Latin players, Chano Pozo, is that because people like were beging to become popular?

That's right, at that time bebop was in good, Chano Pozo you know, and of course made the conga drum very popular, and it was one of those things, and I think the reason why I never, I never kept that band together or it wasn't too popular, because we were far out. We were playing some really modern stuff. We had a theme song with numbered rhythm.
What was that called?
Cozy Cole and his Beepopers.
I'm looking at the discography. It's called Cozy Cole's Cu-boppers.
Cu-boppers, that's it.
And that clarinet player, you couldn't think of his last name is Tony Aquaviva.
Tony Aquaviva that's right, I'm going to write that down, could never think of his name.
I'm going to leave these with you anyway.
Okay, Tony Aquaviva.

Right and you had on bongos Bill Alvarez and Diego Iborra on congas. And apparently you recorded four tunes with that group for the Candy label. You've recorded for some interesting labels, the Love label, Candy label. Let's see, these particular tunes are
"Stardust," "La Dance," "Mosquito Brain," and "Patao."
Yeah, that's right.
And it's in 1949.
Tony Aquaviva, that was his name.
Yeah that must have been an interesting band, it's an unusual instrumentation.
Yeah it was, it was a nice sounding band, I thought. I don't imagine the public did.
Well did you get much work with it?
Yeah we worked rather steady, pretty steady with it, you know.
Probably just the hard times of bee bop.
Yeah, that's right.
When bee-bop came in, did that create problems for you and for the guys that you had grown up with and matured with?

No, because a lot of the guys that I grew up with, you know we still were still bent on just playing that good swing and straight ahead and playing some good music that we liked, and felt, you know and never bothered us at all. I know it never bothered me any
